Proposition ([computer + paper]). \(D_5(Q)=1\) for every \(2\)-group \(Q\) of order \(2^{11}\), class \(3\) and rank \(d(Q)\ge8\).

Proof. Suppose not; then \(Q\) is a candidate, and \(|\Phi(Q)|=2^{11-d}\). Since \(c\ge4\), the strictly decreasing series \(P_2\supsetneq P_3\supsetneq P_4\ne1\) gives \(|\Phi(Q)|\ge8\), so \(d\le8\): rank \(\ge9\) is impossible [paper]. Let \(d=8\). Then, as in the proof of Lemma 5.6, \(c=4\), \(|P_3(Q)|=4\) and \(P_4(Q)=\langle n\rangle\); so \(V=Q/P_3(Q)\) has order \(2^9\), rank \(8\) and \(2\)-class \(2\), and \(R=Q/\langle n\rangle\) is an immediate descendant of step \(1\) of \(V\). Moreover \(R\) has class \(2\): if it had class \(3\), Remark 5.5(ii) applied to \(R\) would give \(d+4e_R+2\le11\) with \(e_R\ge1\), i.e. \(d\le5\) [paper]. [computer] The groups of order \(2^9\) and rank \(8\) are the \(12\) groups SmallGroup\((512,i)\), \(10\,494\,201\le i\le10\,494\,212\) (a group \(V\) of rank \(n\) with \(|\Phi(V)|=2\) is determined by its squaring map \(q\colon V/\Phi(V)\to\Phi(V)\), a nonzero quadratic form on \(\mathbb F_2^n\) whose polar form is the commutator form, so such groups correspond to nonzero quadratic forms up to equivalence; if the polar form has rank \(2k\) and radical \(R\), then \(q|_R=0\) gives two classes for each \(1\le k\le n/2\) (Arf invariant \(0\) or \(1\)) and \(q|_R\ne0\) one class for each \(0\le k<n/2\), so \(2\lfloor n/2\rfloor+\lceil n/2\rceil\) classes, \(12\) for \(n=8\); the same formula gives the numbers of groups of order \(2^{n+1}\) and rank \(n\) in SmallGroups for \(n=2,\dots,7\), namely \(3,4,6,7,9,10\)). Of the \(11\) non-abelian ones, \(10\) have trivial nucleus and hence no immediate descendants at all [OBr90]; for SmallGroup\((512,10\,494\,202)\) the nucleus has dimension \(1\), but every immediate descendant of class \(\le3\) has class \(3\), so it has no descendant \(R\) of class \(2\). Both are read off the \(p\)-covering group, without computing automorphism groups; the two rules and their proofs are in compute/pq2048/README.md (section “Vertices without descendants”, Rules \(0\) and \(2\)) [paper], checked there against full ANUPQ expansion. The remaining group SmallGroup\((512,10\,494\,201)\cong\mathbb{Z}/4\times(\mathbb{Z}/2)^7\) is excluded by Lemma 5.6.

An independent check of rank \(8\) by direct generation agrees: on \(\mathbb{Z}/4\times(\mathbb{Z}/2)^7\) the stock ANUPQ is estimated to need about \(20\) GB (a run was killed at \(7\) GB), while a version with a memory fix completes it in \(2.1\) GB, finding \(8\) immediate descendants of order \(2^{10}\); the walk from all \(12\) groups then gives no candidate of order \(2^{11}\) [computer].

Central products. A search beyond order \(2^{11}\) may skip candidates that split as central products with a small factor. Let \(E\) be a finite \(2\)-group of class \(2\) with \(E/Z(E)\cong(\mathbb{Z}/2)^2\) and cyclic centre. Replacing \(E\) by the subgroup generated by two lifts \(a,b\) of a basis of \(E/Z(E)\), which does not change the central product below, one has \(E\in\{D_8,Q_8\}\) or \(E\cong M_{2^{k+2}}=\langle a,b\mid a^{2^{k+1}}=b^2=1,\ a^b=a^{1+2^k}\rangle\), \(k\ge2\), with \(Z(E)=\langle a^2\rangle\) [paper]. For an embedding \(\varphi\colon Z(E)\to Z(H)\) let \(H\circ E=(H\times E)/\{(\varphi(z),z^{-1})\}\), \(t=\varphi([a,b])\) and, for \(E=M_{2^{k+2}}\), \(s=\varphi(a^2)\).

Proposition ([Lean]). Let \(H\) be a group with \(t\in\gamma_2(H)\), and \(n\ge2\). • If \(E\in\{D_8,Q_8\}\), then \(D_n(H\circ E)=D_n(H)\). • If \(E=M_{2^{k+2}}\) and for some \(g\in H\) the element \(c=g^{-2}s\) satisfies \(c^{2^j}-1\in\Delta(H)^{j+2}\) for all \(j\ge0\) (for instance \(c^{2^j}\in\gamma_{j+2}(H)\)), then \(D_n(H\circ E)=D_n(H)\). This holds in particular if \(s=g^2\) for some \(g\in H\), central or not (\(c=1\)), and if \(s\in\gamma_2(H)\), \(s^2\in\gamma_3(H)\) (\(g=1\), \(k=2\)).

Proof. Let \(Q\ge H\) be one of the groups below, generated by \(H\) and elements commuting with \(H\), and \(\gamma_2(Q)=\gamma_2(H)\). Then \(D_n(Q)\subseteq\gamma_2(Q)\subseteq H\) and \(D_n(H)\subseteq D_n(Q)\), so \(D_n(Q)=D_n(H)\) follows once \(\mathbb{Z}[H]\cap\Delta(Q)^n\subseteq\Delta(H)^n\). For that it suffices to have a left \(\mathbb{Z}[H]\)-linear \(q\colon\mathbb{Z}[Q]\to\mathbb{Z}[H]\), the identity on \(\mathbb{Z}[H]\), with \(q(\Delta(Q)^n)\subseteq\Delta(H)^n\). Here \(\gamma_2(H\circ E)=\gamma_2(H)\langle t\rangle=\gamma_2(H)\).

(1) Let \(E=D_8\), \(c=[a,b]\), \(\tau=c-1\) (so \(\tau^2=-2\tau\)), and \(N=\mathbb{Z}[E/\langle b\rangle]\), free over \(\mathbb{Z}[\langle c\rangle]\) on \(e_0\) and \(f=ae_0-e_0\). Then \(\mathbb{Z}[H]\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}[\langle c\rangle]}N\) is a \(\mathbb{Z}[Q]\)-module, and \(q(u)=(\mathrm{id}\otimes p)(u(1\otimes e_0))\) with \(p(xe_0+yf)=x\) is as required. Indeed, \(\Delta(Q)^n\) is spanned by products of \(i\) factors from \(\Delta(H)\) and \(n-i\) from \(\Delta(E)\), and on \(N\) in the coordinates \((x,y)\) one has \(a-1\colon(x,y)\mapsto(0,x-2y)\) and \(b-1\colon(x,y)\mapsto(\tau y,\tau y)\). By induction, \(p(\Delta(E)^jN)=\tau^{\lceil j/2\rceil}\mathbb{Z}[\langle c\rangle]\) for \(j\ge1\); as \(t-1\in\Delta(H)^2\), \(q(\Delta(Q)^n)\subseteq\sum_i\Delta(H)^i(t-1)^{\lceil(n-i)/2\rceil}\subseteq\Delta(H)^n\). For \(Q_8\): \(u=ab\in D_8\) has \(u^2=t\), so \(H'=H\langle u\rangle\le H\circ D_8\) and \(D_n(H')=D_n(H)\). If \(a',b'\) are the generators of the factor \(D_8\) of \(H'\circ D_8\), the elements \(a'u,b'u\) generate a \(Q_8\) meeting \(H'\) in \(\langle t\rangle\), so \(H\circ Q_8\le H'\circ D_8\) and \(D_n(H\circ Q_8)\subseteq D_n(H')\cap H=D_n(H)\), using (1) for \(H'\).

(2) Let \(H''=H\langle r\rangle\) with \(r\) central, \(r^2=s\), \(\langle r\rangle\cap H=\langle s\rangle\). With \(a',b'\) the generators of the factor \(D_8\) of \(H''\circ D_8\), the elements \(a'r,b'\) generate a copy of \(E\) meeting \(H''\) in \(\langle s\rangle\), and \(H\langle a\rangle\cong H''\) inside \(H\circ E\); by (1), \(D_n(H\circ E)=D_n(H'')\). Now \(\mathbb{Z}[H'']=\mathbb{Z}[H]\oplus\mathbb{Z}[H]r\); put \(q(u_0+u_1r)=u_0+u_1g\). As \(r\) is central, \(\Delta(H'')^n=\sum_i\Delta(H)^{n-i}(r-1)^i\mathbb{Z}[H'']\), so it suffices that \(f_i=q((r-1)^i)\in\Delta(H)^i\) for all \(i\). In the abelian group \(\langle g,s,r\rangle\) put \(y=rg^{-1}\), so \(y^2=c\), and \(x=g-1\), \(\eta=y-1\), \(\tau=c-1\). Then \(r-1=x+\eta+x\eta\) and \(f_i=\sum_{\alpha+\beta\ge i}m_{\alpha\beta}\,x^\alpha e_\beta\) with \(e_b=\pi(\eta^b)\), \(\pi(v_0+v_1y)=v_0+v_1\). From \(\eta^2=\tau-2\eta\) we get \(e_1=0\), \(e_2=\tau\) and \(e_{b+2}=\tau e_b-2e_{b+1}\). The identity \(2(c^{2^j}-1)=(c^{2^{j+1}}-1)-(c^{2^j}-1)^2\) and the hypothesis give \(2^m\tau\in\Delta(H)^{m+2}\) for all \(m\). Hence, by induction on \(b\ge1\), \(2^me_b\in\Delta(H)^{b+m}\) for all \(m\); in particular \(e_b\in\Delta(H)^b\).

The condition \(c\in\gamma_2(H)\), i.e. \(s\in\Phi(H)\) for a \(2\)-group, cannot be dropped from the method: if \(s\notin\Phi(H)\), no such \(q\) for \(H''\) satisfies \(q(\Delta(H'')^2)\subseteq\Delta(H)^2\) [paper]. [computer] For the \(386\) candidates \(H\) of orders \(2^6\)–\(2^9\), \(t=n\in\gamma_3(H)\). The \(291\) with \(|Z(H)|\ge8\) have \(s\) a square in the cyclic \(Z(H)\). Of the \(95\) with \(Z(H)\cong\mathbb{Z}/4\), \(78\) have \(s\in\gamma_2(H)\) and \(s^2\in\gamma_3(H)\), and the other \(17\) have \(s=g^2\) with \(g\in H\) not central. So by Proposition 5.8, \(D_n(H\circ E)=D_n(H)\) for all of them, all \(n\) and \(E\in\{D_8,Q_8,M_{16}\}\). Independently, the lattice computation gives \(D_4=D_5=1\) for all \(1\,544\) such products.

Gluing along a proper subgroup. For \(C\le Z(E)\) and an embedding \(\varphi\colon C\to Z(H)\) let \(H\circ_CE=(H\times E)/\{(\varphi(z),z^{-1})\colon z\in C\}\). Then \(H'=HZ(E)\) centralises \(E\), \(H\circ_CE=H'\circ E\) is a gluing along all of \(Z(E)\) (with \(\varphi\) the inclusion, so \(s=a^2\in H'\) for \(E=M_{2^{k+2}}\)), and \(\gamma_i(H')=\gamma_i(H)\) for \(i\ge2\). For \(E=M_{2^{k+2}}\), \(H'\circ E\) can be written as \(H\circ_CE\) with \(C\ne Z(E)\) exactly when \(s\notin\Phi(H')\), which is where the method of part (2) for \(H'\) fails by the remark above. The projection then has to go to \(H\) instead of \(H'\).

Lemma ([Lean]). Let \(K=H\langle r\rangle\) with \(r\) central, \(|K:H|=m\), and \(r^m=\sigma=g^m\) for some \(g\in H\), not necessarily central. Then \(\mathbb{Z}[H]\cap\Delta(K)^n=\Delta(H)^n\) for all \(n\), and \(D_n(K)=D_n(H)\) for \(n\ge2\).

Proof. \(\mathbb{Z}[K]=\bigoplus_{0\le j<m}\mathbb{Z}[H]r^j\); put \(q(\sum_ju_jr^j)=\sum_ju_jg^j\). As \(r^m=g^m\in H\), \(q(ur^j)=ug^j\) for all \(j\in\mathbb{Z}\), so \(q(u\,p(r))=u\,p(g)\) for every Laurent polynomial \(p\). As \(r\) is central, \(\Delta(K)^n\) is spanned by the \(x(r-1)^ir^j\) with \(x\in\Delta(H)^{n-i}\), and \(q(x(r-1)^ir^j)=x(g-1)^ig^j\in\Delta(H)^n\). Hence \(\mathbb{Z}[H]\cap\Delta(K)^n=q(\mathbb{Z}[H]\cap\Delta(K)^n)\subseteq\Delta(H)^n\); the reverse inclusion is clear, and \(D_n(K)\subseteq\gamma_2(K)=\gamma_2(H)\subseteq H\) gives the rest.

For \(m=2\) this is the case \(c=1\) of Proposition 5.8(2). Let \(E=M_{2^{k+2}}\), \(C=\langle a^{2^{j+1}}\rangle\) with \(1\le j<k\), and \(\sigma=\varphi(a^{2^{j+1}})\). If \(t\in\gamma_2(H)\) and \(\sigma=g^{2^{j+1}}\) for some \(g\in H\), then \(D_n(H\circ_CE)=D_n(H)\) for \(n\ge2\) [paper]: in the proof of (2) for \(H'\) one has \(H''=H'\langle r\rangle=H\langle r\rangle\) with \(r^{2^{j+1}}=\sigma\) and \(\langle r\rangle\cap H=\langle\sigma\rangle\), so \(|H'':H|=2^{j+1}\), and Lemma 5.9 applies with \(m=2^{j+1}\). For instance, \(H\circ_{\langle t\rangle}M_{16}\) needs \(t=g^4\). The hypothesis \(t\in\gamma_2(H)\) costs nothing for the search: if \(H\circ_CE\) is a candidate, \(t\) is the involution of its cyclic centre, so \(t=n\in\gamma_3(H\circ_CE)=\gamma_3(H)\). [computer] Of the \(386\) candidates of orders \(2^6\)–\(2^9\), \(20\) split as central products (\(5\) of order \(2^8\), \(15\) of order \(2^9\)), with \(212\) factors \(E\) in all. The gluing is proper in \(16\) of these splittings, belonging to \(4\) candidates, always with \(M_{32}\) or \(M_{64}\); Lemma 5.9 covers \(4\) of them. Each of the \(20\) candidates also has a splitting covered by Proposition 5.8, so at these orders a search that skips split candidates does not need proper gluing (code: compute/central, decomp.g; wiki, MATH-186). The other \(12\) splittings would need an analogue of (2) for \(m=4\) (taking \(H\) maximal in \(H'\), i.e. \(j=1\)) with \(g^{-4}\sigma\ne1\); it cannot go through a projection to \(H\) in general, since for \(Q=D_8\circ_{\langle t\rangle}M_{16}\) one has \(\mathbb{Z}[D_8]\cap\Delta(Q)^n\ne\Delta(D_8)^n\) at \(n=4,5\) (index \(4\)), although \(D_n(Q)=D_n(D_8)\) [computer] [open].

\(3\)-torsion. For \(3\)-torsion the computation is no longer needed up to order \(3^7\) (Theorem 5.4(3)); orders \(3^8\) and \(3^9\) and an infinite family are treated in §6. Quotients of the known examples (Rips, \(D_4\ne\gamma_4\) at order \(2^{38}\); Bartholdi–Mikhailov at order \(3^{494}\)) could calibrate how far a counterexample to Question 1.1 must be.

Order \(2^{11}\), all ranks. Proposition ([computer + paper; uses Tahara 1977, Cor. 19]). \(D_5(Q)=1\) for every \(2\)-group \(Q\) of order \(2^{11}\) and class \(3\). Hence a counterexample to Question 1.1 among finite \(2\)-groups of class \(3\) has order at least \(2^{12}\). Proof. A \(2\)-group of order \(2^{11}\) and class \(3\) with \(D_5\ne1\) is a candidate (above). Ranks \(\ge8\): Proposition 5.7. Ranks \(2\)–\(7\): the searches above find every candidate of these ranks except, at ranks \(5\) and \(6\), those dropped by rule (T), which have \(D_5=1\); all the candidates found have \(D_5=1\). Rank \(1\): cyclic groups are abelian. Orders below \(2^{11}\): Propositions 5.1 and 5.3. See also the remark on the ANUPQ versions above.

Theorem 5.4(3) settles \(3\)-torsion up to order \(3^7\) by metabelianity. Here we go further: we prove \(D_5=\gamma_5\) for all \(3\)-groups of order \(\le 3^9\) (Theorem 6.12) and, on paper, for every finite \(3\)-group \(Q\) with \(Q/\gamma_2(Q)\) of exponent \(3\), of any order (Theorem 6.6). Details, the computations and two independent line-by-line reviews are in our wiki (MATH-120, MATH-127); code in compute/magnus. Throughout, the type of a group \(Q\) of class \(c\) is \((a_1,\dots,a_c)\) with \(p^{a_i}=|\gamma_i(Q)/\gamma_{i+1}(Q)|\), and \(L(Q)=\bigoplus_i\gamma_i/\gamma_{i+1}\) is its Lie ring.
section: 6. \(3\)-torsion: orders \(3^8\) and \(3^9\), and groups with \(G/\gamma_2\) of exponent \(3\)

text: Lemma. Let \(p\) be odd and \(Q\) a finite \(p\)-group of class \(\le p+1\). Then \(D_{p+2}(Q)\subseteq Q''\cap M_{p+2}(Q)\). In particular, for \(p=3\) and class \(\le4\), \(D_5(Q)\subseteq Q''\cap M_5(Q)\), and \(D_5(Q)\ne1\) needs \(Q''\ne1\), hence \(d(Q)\ge3\).
section: 6. \(3\)-torsion: orders \(3^8\) and \(3^9\), and groups with \(G/\gamma_2\) of exponent \(3\)

text: Proof. \(Q/Q''\) is metabelian of class \(\le p+1\), so \(D_{p+2}(Q/Q'')=\gamma_{p+2}(Q/Q'')=1\) by [GT85, Thm. 3.2], and \(D_{p+2}(Q)\subseteq Q''\) by functoriality. \(D_n\subseteq M_n\) because \(\mathbb{Z}[Q]\to\mathbb F_p[Q]\) maps \(\Delta^n\) into \(\Delta_{\mathbb F_p}^n\). If \(d(Q)\le2\) then \(\gamma_2/\gamma_3\) is cyclic and \(Q''\subseteq\gamma_5=1\) (see Lemma 6.3).

text: Lemma. [minimal counterexample, \(p=3\)] Let \(Q\) be a \(3\)-group of least order with \(D_5(Q)\ne\gamma_5(Q)\). Then \(Q\) has class \(4\), \(Q''\ne1\) and \(d(Q)\ge3\); \(Z(Q)\) is cyclic and \(D_5(Q)=\Omega_1(Z(Q))=\langle z\rangle\) has order \(3\), with \(z\in Q''\cap M_5(Q)\); the last nontrivial term \(P_c(Q)\) of the lower exponent-\(3\) central series equals \(\langle z\rangle\), so \(Q\) is an immediate descendant of step size \(1\) of \(Q/\langle z\rangle\).

text: Proof. If \(Q\) had class \(\ge5\), then \(Q/\gamma_5(Q)\) would be a smaller counterexample; for class \(\le3\), \(D_5\subseteq D_4=\gamma_4=1\) (Passi: \(D_4=\gamma_4\) without \(2\)-torsion [Pas68]). So \(Q\) has class \(4\), and Lemma 6.1 gives \(1\ne D_5(Q)\subseteq Q''\cap M_5(Q)\). The rest is the argument of Lemma 5.2: \(D_5(Q)\) lies in every normal \(N\) with \(D_5(Q/N)=1\), in particular in every central subgroup of order \(3\).
section: 6. \(3\)-torsion: orders \(3^8\) and \(3^9\), and groups with \(G/\gamma_2\) of exponent \(3\)

text: Lemma. Let \(p\) be odd and \(G\) a group with \(|\gamma_3(G)/\gamma_4(G)|=p\) and \(\gamma_2(G)/\gamma_3(G)\) generated by at most two elements. Then \([\gamma_2(G),\gamma_2(G)]\subseteq\gamma_5(G)\). In particular, \(G\) is metabelian if it has class \(\le4\).

Proof. [Proof [paper; Lean] (in Lean the same computation is done in the group \(G/\gamma_5(G)\), §4)] The image of \([\gamma_2,\gamma_2]\) in \(\gamma_4/\gamma_5\) is spanned by the brackets \([L_2,L_2]\subseteq L_4\) of \(L=L(G)\), so it suffices to show \([L_2,L_2]=0\). If \(L_2\) is cyclic, the alternating bracket \(L_2\times L_2\to L_4\) vanishes. Otherwise \(pL_3=0\), hence \(pL_4=0\) (\(L_4=[L_3,L_1]\)), and dividing \(L\) by the ideal \(pL_1\oplus pL_2\oplus0\oplus H\oplus L_{\ge5}\), where \(H\subset L_4\) is a hyperplane missing a given nonzero bracket \([u,v]\), we get a graded \(\mathbb F_p\)-Lie algebra \(M=M_1\oplus\dots\oplus M_4\) generated by \(M_1\) with \(\dim M_2=2\), \(\dim M_3=\dim M_4=1\) and \([M_2,M_2]\ne0\). We show that this is impossible.

Write \([z,z']=\omega(z,z')w\) for \(z,z'\in M_2\), \(M_4=\langle w\rangle\), \(M_3=\langle t\rangle\), \([x,t]=\varphi(x)w\), \([x,z]=\beta(x,z)t\) and \([x,y]=\alpha(x,y)\) for \(x,y\in M_1\), \(z\in M_2\). A nonzero alternating form on a plane is nondegenerate, so \(\omega\) is; \(\varphi\ne0\) since \(M_4=[M_1,M_3]\). Pick \(e\) with \(\varphi(e)=1\) and let \(K=\ker\varphi\). The Jacobi identity for \(x,y\in M_1\), \(z\in M_2\) reads \[\omega(\alpha(x,y),z)=\varphi(x)\beta(y,z)-\varphi(y)\beta(x,z).\] For \(x,y\in K\) the right side vanishes, so \(\alpha(K,K)=0\) and \(M_2=\alpha(e,K)\); for \(x=e\), \(y=k\in K\) it gives \(\beta(k,z)=\omega(\alpha(e,k),z)\). The Jacobi identity for \(e,k_1,k_2\in K\), with \(u_i=\alpha(e,k_i)\) and \(\alpha(k_1,k_2)=0\), gives \(\beta(k_1,u_2)-\beta(k_2,u_1)=0\), i.e. \(2\,\omega(u_1,u_2)=0\). As \(p\ne2\) and the \(u_i\) run over \(M_2\), \(\omega=0\), a contradiction.
An independent proof for \(|\gamma_2/\gamma_3|=p^2\) (both forms \(\omega_1,\omega_2\) of \([L_1,L_1]\to L_2\) and an exterior-algebra computation) is in the wiki (MATH-127, part 3).

Remark. • The hypothesis \(p\ne2\) is needed: SmallGroup\((128,i)\), \(i=928,\dots,937\), have type \((3,2,1,1)\) and \(|G''|=2\), and there are \(108\) such groups of order \(2^8\) [computer]. • The other two hypotheses are sharp at order \(3^8\): of the \(904\) non-metabelian \(3\)-groups of class \(4\) and order \(3^8\), \(15\) have type \((3,3,1,1)\) and \(889\) type \((3,2,2,1)\) [computer]; an explicit Lie algebra of type \((3,3,1,1)\) with \([M_2,M_2]\ne0\) is in the wiki [paper]. • Check: for all groups of orders \(3^5\)–\(3^8\) of class \(\ge4\) the hypothesis holds in \(13\,077\) groups and the conclusion in all of them; a referee's scan of all \(1\,396\,077\) groups of order \(3^8\) and all groups of order \(7^7\) found \(24\,215\) and \(4\,408\) groups with \(|\gamma_2/\gamma_3|=p^2\), \(|\gamma_3/\gamma_4|=p\), and no violation [computer].

Proposition. [[Lean]; the examples for \(p=3\): [computer]] Let \(p\) be odd and \(Q\) a \(p\)-group of class \(4\). • If \(|Q|\le p^7\), or \(|Q|=p^8\) and \(d(Q)\ge4\), then \(Q\) is metabelian. • If \(|Q|=p^9\) and \(Q''\ne1\), then \(d(Q)\in\{3,4\}\); for \(d(Q)=4\) the type is \((4,3,1,1)\) or \((4,2,2,1)\), and for \(p=3\) both occur (\(Q_0\times C_3\) with \(Q_0\) of order \(3^8\) as in Remark 6.4(2)).

Proof. Let \((a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4)\) be the type. By Lemma 6.3, \(Q''\ne1\) needs \(a_3\ge2\) or \(\gamma_2/\gamma_3\) with at least three generators; as \(\gamma_2/\gamma_3\) is not cyclic, \(a_2\ge2\), so \(a_2\ge3\) or \(a_3\ge2\). Moreover \(a_1\ge d(Q)\), \(a_4\ge1\), and for \(d(Q)=2\) the group \(\gamma_2/\gamma_3\) is cyclic. So \(d(Q)\ge3\) and \(|Q|\ge p^{d(Q)+5}\), which gives (1) and the first part of (2); at \(p^9\) and \(d=4\) the bound is attained exactly by the two types listed. At \(p^9\) and \(d=5\) the only type with \(a_2\ge2\) is \((5,2,1,1)\), and such groups are metabelian.

In particular the computer statement “every \(3\)-group of class \(4\) and order \(3^5\), \(3^6\), \(3^7\) is metabelian” of Proposition 5.1 now has a proof, and so does the observation that all non-metabelian groups of class \(4\) and order \(3^8\) have rank \(3\).

Theorem. [[paper; Lean]; relies on [Tah81, Thm. 6.1], also formalized] Let \(Q\) be a finite \(3\)-group with \(Q/\gamma_2(Q)\) of exponent \(3\). Then \(D_5(Q)=\gamma_5(Q)\). More generally, \(D_5(G)=\gamma_5(G)\) for every group \(G\) with \(G/\gamma_2(G)\) finite of exponent \(3\).
